t.1.102.1: When those three boys were born, Kurujāṅgala, the Kurus, and Kurukṣetra, these three, prospered.
t.1.102.2: The earth bore tall-standing crops, and the crops were rich in fruit; Parjanya rained in due season, and the trees were laden with abundant flowers and fruit.
t.1.102.3: The draft animals were joyful, the beasts and birds were glad, the garlands were fragrant, and the fruits were full of flavor.
t.1.102.4: The cities were then filled with merchants and with artisans; the brave, the learned, and the virtuous were happy.
t.1.102.5: There were no robbers at all, nor were there people who delighted in unrighteousness; even in the outlying regions of the kingdoms, the Kṛta age prevailed.
t.1.102.6: Devoted to charity, sacred rites and dharma, intent upon sacrifices and vows, and bound together by mutual affection, the people then prospered and increased.
t.1.102.7: The people, free of pride and anger and devoid of greed, helped one another to prosper, and all things proceeded with dharma foremost.
t.1.102.8: That city, full like the great ocean, shone forth indeed, furnished with gates, arched portals and turrets resembling masses of clouds, crowded with hundreds of palaces, like the city of great Indra.
t.1.102.9: By the rivers, in the stretches of woodland, at the wells, ponds and mountain slopes, and in delightful forests, the joyful people took their pleasure.
t.1.102.10: At that time the Southern Kurus roamed about, vying with the Northern Kurus, and likewise with the Siddhas, Ṛṣis and Cāraṇas. No one was wretched, and no women were widows.
t.1.102.12: That land became delightful, marked with hundreds of shrines and sacrificial posts, and it grew, having taken in the kingdoms of others. The wheel of dharma established by Bhīṣma turned throughout the kingdom.
t.1.102.11: In that delightful country, guarded on every side by Bhīṣma in accordance with the śāstras, O king, the Kurus made many wells, gardens, assembly halls and ponds, and likewise dwellings for brāhmaṇas.
t.1.102.13: While the rites and duties for the high-souled princes were being performed, all the people of the city and the countryside were in continual festivity.
t.1.102.14: In the houses of the foremost of the Kurus and of the townsfolk, O lord of men, the words "Let it be given, and let it be eaten!" were heard everywhere.
t.1.102.15: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and the greatly wise Vidura were cared for by Bhīṣma like sons from their very birth.
t.1.102.16: Consecrated with the sacraments, devoted to vows and Vedic study, and skilled in toil and physical exercise, they reached the bloom of youth.
t.1.102.17: They became masters of the science of archery, of horsemanship, of fighting with the mace, of sword and shield, and likewise of the training of elephants and of the science of statecraft.
t.1.102.18: O mighty one, they knew the true essence of the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, and had devoted diligent effort everywhere, in the Itihāsas and Purāṇas and in the various branches of learning.
t.1.102.19: Pāṇḍu, valorous with the bow, became superior to all other men; Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the earth, was mighty beyond all others.
t.1.102.20: In the three worlds there was no one equal to Vidura, ever devoted to dharma; thus, O king, he had attained the highest state in dharma.
t.1.102.22: Among mothers of heroes, the two daughters of the king of Kāśi were foremost; among lands, Kurujāṅgala; among all knowers of dharma, Bhīṣma; and among cities, Gajasāhvaya.
t.1.102.21: Seeing that the lineage of Śaṃtanu, which had perished, was raised up once more, a saying then spread through the world, in all the kingdoms.
t.1.102.23: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, because of his blindness, did not obtain the kingdom, nor did Vidura, because of his mixed birth; so Pāṇḍu became lord of the earth.
